newsitem.title: DUBAI: Mideast Gulf oil outlooks - winter buying ebbs.
newsitem.headline: Mideast Gulf oil outlooks - winter buying ebbs.

text.p: Gulf oil product prices have found a short-term floor but are unlikely to strike higher since Asian consumers had now secured most of their winter fuel needs, oil traders based in the Gulf said on Thursday.
With February deliveries largely in place, the chance of a bullish cold snap in key Japanese, South Korean and other Asian import markets was becoming slimmer, they said.
"Winter buying is coming to a close. Activity is already down," one trader in the region said.
Saudi Aramco on Thursday cut the price of February propane by $10 a tonne to $320 and butane by $25 to $305, still higher than the year-on-year comparisons of $205 and $188.
Jet-kerosene was assessed at $28.80 a barrel fob Gulf on Thursday, up $2.45 on the week based on firmer Singapore February heating markets. Its premium was unchanged at 50 cents.

Gas oil (diesel) failed to match the gains in heating fuel, losing 20 cents to $23.25 fob Gulf. Premiums for 0.5 percent sulphur material were assessed at 60-70 cents and 50-55 cents for one percent sulphur grade.
The jet-gas oil spread at $5.55 is at its widest since January 1996.

Middle distillate premiums would also be shaped by a buying tender from Oman Refinery Company to cover domestic supplies during a six-week-long maintenance programme at its 75,000 barrels per day (bpd) Mina al Fahal refinery, traders said.
Oman has invited bids for the supply of the equivalent of 94,000 tonnes of gasoline, 31,500 tonnes of jet and 67,500 tonnes of one percent sulphur gas oil, traders said.
The cargoes are for delivery in eight combination cargoes spread between February and April.
Premiums would also be shaped by India Oil Corp's (IOC) upcoming tender for kerosene and the level of the state firm's diesel purchases during the next financial year starting April.
"IOC has kept its buying activity at a minimum over the last months because of fiscal pressures...But in the new year (April) buying should be stronger," a trader said.
IOC bought 15 diesel cargoes totalling 615,000 tonnes in its tender for March delivery, within market expectations.
Naphtha prices and premiums also made ground on firmer Asian petrochemical markets, gaining $2 cents in the week to $208 a tonne fob Gulf and a $13 premium to independent price quotes.
